meta.sources: Sources: course pages on [Coursera](https://www.coursera.org), [edX](https://www.edx.org), [CDC TRAIN](https://www.train.org/cdctrain/), [OpenWHO](https://openwho.org/), CDC, Harvard CCDD, [Operation Outbreak](https://operationoutbreak.org/resources), and [FutureLearn](https://www.futurelearn.com). Newsletter and podcast picks follow the [Emerging Technology Policy Careers biosecurity guide](https://emergingtechpolicy.org/areas/biosecurity-policy/), [ProMED](https://www.promedmail.org/), and [GCBR Organization Updates](https://gcbrupdates.substack.com/).

courses.name: Operation Outbreak: Lessons and Activities
courses.note: Free, ready-to-use outbreak science resources: 17 lesson plans with activities and simulations, the 16-episode Crash Course: Outbreak Science video series, and an open-access 13-chapter textbook. Built for high-school classrooms; useful to anyone starting out.

courses.name: Crash Course: Outbreak Science
courses.org: Crash Course (YouTube), hosted by Pardis Sabeti
courses.note: Sixteen short, friendly videos from what an outbreak is to how one ends. Pair it with the Public Health series.

courses.name: Principles of Epidemiology in Public Health Practice
courses.note: Free, self-paced, six lessons from Introduction to Epidemiology to Investigating an Outbreak, with exercises and quizzes. The textbook the field's practitioners learned from.

courses.name: Outbreaks and Epidemics
courses.note: About five hours, free to audit. How to ask precise epidemiologic questions and investigate an outbreak, with case studies from Ebola in West Africa to the US opioid epidemic.

courses.name: Next Generation Biosecurity: Responding to 21st Century Biorisks
courses.org: University of Bath and Biosecure, FutureLearn
courses.note: Six weeks, four hours a week, online; free to join with an optional paid certificate. The biosecurity side of the field: biosafety, biosecurity, and bioethics inside and outside the lab.

newsletters.name: GCBR Organization Updates
newsletters.note: Round-ups of what organizations working on global catastrophic biological risks are doing, including openings, fellowships, and courses.

newsletters.name: ProMED
newsletters.note: A 24/7 early-warning system for emerging infectious diseases, running for more than 30 years; it reported early on SARS, MERS, Zika, and COVID-19. Human experts review 5 to 20 events a day. Check the site for current subscription terms.

newsletters.name: BEACON
newsletters.org: Boston University Center on Emerging Infectious Diseases, with the Hariri Institute, Boston Children's Hospital, and HealthMap
newsletters.note: An open, searchable feed of curated disease-event reports from around the world, updated daily and filterable by pathogen, disease, region, and species. Read it alongside ProMED to learn how outbreaks are first noticed.

newsletters.name: Health Security Decoded
newsletters.org: Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security (monthly)

newsletters.name: CIDRAP Daily Headlines
newsletters.org: Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy

newsletters.name: Resilience Action Playbook
newsletters.org: Resilience Action Network International, formerly the Pandemic Action Network

podcasts.name: This Podcast Will Kill You
podcasts.note: Disease history and biology, one pathogen per episode.

podcasts.name: Poisons and Pestilence
podcasts.note: History of chemical and biological weapons.

podcasts.name: Hear This Idea and the 80,000 Hours Podcast

outbreakTraining.name: OpenWHO
outbreakTraining.note: WHO's free learning hub for health emergencies: no registration, no certificates, just the material. Includes the Rapid Response Teams training program, the Emergency Response Framework, mass casualty management, and introductory courses on specific diseases from Ebola to MERS.

outbreakTraining.name: Introduction to Outbreak Investigation
outbreakTraining.note: One hour, introductory, free with a TRAIN account. The steps for deciding whether you have an outbreak, who investigates, the science behind it, and how to tell the public.

outbreakTraining.name: Risk Communication in Public Health Emergencies
outbreakTraining.note: Two hours, intermediate, free with a TRAIN account. Case-based practice in building risk and crisis messages before and during an emergency. For the Communication track.

outbreakTraining.name: Epidemics I
outbreakTraining.org: University of Hong Kong on edX
outbreakTraining.note: Five weeks at two to three hours a week, free to audit. Origins of novel pathogens, ecology and emergence of infectious diseases, and 'medical detective' work, with a COVID-19 module. First of a four-course series.

outbreakTraining.name: Lessons from Ebola: Preventing the Next Pandemic
outbreakTraining.note: Four weeks at three to five hours a week, free to audit. What went right and wrong in the West Africa Ebola response, told by practitioners and scholars. More than 100,000 learners have enrolled.

outbreakTraining.name: Epidemiology: The Basic Science of Public Health
outbreakTraining.org: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill on Coursera
outbreakTraining.note: About seven hours, free to audit. How disease patterns are studied and used to control public-health problems, with infectious-disease and cardiovascular examples.

outbreakTraining.name: Epidemiology in Public Health Practice
outbreakTraining.note: Five courses over four to five months, paid with financial aid available. The core epidemiologic toolset: measuring population health, assessing interventions, collecting and analyzing data, and investigating outbreaks. The most complete free-standing introduction short of a degree.

outbreakTraining.name: Introduction to Infectious Disease Modeling
outbreakTraining.org: Harvard T.H. Chan Center for Communicable Disease Dynamics
outbreakTraining.note: Free recorded lectures from a Harvard course, made public during COVID-19. For the Data & Technology track.

outbreakTraining.name: One Health Lessons
outbreakTraining.note: Free science lessons on how the health of people, animals, plants, and the environment connect, taught worldwide to children and adults. Volunteers can train as Lesson Leaders and teach the lessons themselves. For the One Health & Environment track.

biosecurityTraining.name: Biosecurity Fundamentals Course
biosecurityTraining.note: Free, remote, about 30 hours, cohort-based. The technical and policy efforts to prevent, detect, and respond to catastrophic pandemics.
